items.claim: The dateline note on MT 1:1 puts its denial behind a comma: the year is given, then a comma, then the statement that the book names no era for it. A denial standing in that position on a dateline claim is a rewording order, not a pass. A second fact in the same row: the parenthetical saying that the transport-verb and the 'he said to me' sweeps begin only at chapter 8 holds for the transport verb, whose earliest verse is MT 8:3, and fails for 'he said to me', which already stands at MT 2:1, MT 3:1, MT 3:3, MT 3:4 and MT 3:10. Everything else the row asserts is true on the bytes: both datelines, the third-person word-event at MT 1:3 under the ruled any-form count of 49, the hand construct as one of the seven, the single closed-section mark after MT 1:28, both paseq verses, the variant site at MT 1:8 and the editorial note at MT 1:11, with nothing in the span left undisclosed.

suggested_fix.fact: the thirtieth year of MT 1:1 stands with no era named for it anywhere in the book, put as its own statement rather than appended after a comma

items.claim: The row holds the two open-section marks inside its span as non-cutting on the stated ground that neither coincides with a formula onset. Both do. The mark on MT 2:2 is followed at MT 2:3 by the speech opening and the address to the prophet, and the mark on MT 2:5 is followed at MT 2:6 by the same 'and you, son of man' address whose first word at MT 2:8 the row itself calls the fresh sub-onset opening the next unit; the first word is byte-identical at MT 2:6 and MT 2:8. A second fact: the translation sentence cited at web:Ezek.2.1 stops at the prophet's feet, while the Hebrew splice beside it runs on through the promise to speak with him, so the two extents differ, and the sentence is given with a lower-case opening where the translation reads it capitalized.
items.both_sides: Near side of the MT 2:7/2:8 junction: MT 2:7 ends on the short form of the refrain, without the word for house, and an open-section mark follows it. Far side: MT 2:8 turns the speech from the audience's obduracy to hearing and eating the scroll. The same pairing of an open-section mark with an address formula stands at the MT 2:5/2:6 junction, where MT 2:6 instead ends on the full refrain and carries the do-not-fear charge forward. So the mark together with the address formula does not separate the two junctions; the change of subject at MT 2:8 does. The boundary stands where the row puts it, on a ground the row does not yet state.

suggested_fix.fact: both open-section marks inside the span stand immediately before an address formula, so what holds them non-cutting is the do-not-fear charge running on through MT 2:6 and MT 2:7, not an absence of formula onset

items.claim: Two splices in this row cover more words than the renderings set beside them. At MT 2:9 the splice opens on the seeing verb and closes on a second presentative particle, while the rendering covers only the hand stretched out; the opening verb and that trailing particle go unrendered, and the particle is cut away from the scroll clause that completes it. At MT 2:10 the splice opens at the pronoun that means in it, severed from the passive participle that governs it, while the rendering covers only the three nouns that follow. The rest of the row holds: the closed-section mark on MT 2:10 and the open-section mark on MT 3:3 are both true and both disclosed, the span carries no paseq and no variant site, and declining a seam at the translation's chapter numeral is right on the marks, since the junction the row does cut carries the open mark and the one it holds through carries the closed one.

suggested_fix.fact: the splice at MT 2:9 runs only over the hand stretched out to the prophet, and the splice at MT 2:10 begins at the participle governing the three nouns, so each splice and its rendering cover the same words

items.claim: The refrain at MT 3:9 is the fourth naming of the rebellious house in chapters 2-3, not the third. The sweep that yields the row set's own twelve book-wide and six in chapters 2-3 puts them at MT 2:5, MT 2:6, MT 2:8, MT 3:9, MT 3:26 and MT 3:27, and the row covering MT 3:22-3:27 counts four of them standing before MT 3:16 and two after, which makes MT 3:9 the fourth on that same arithmetic. The ordinal here therefore contradicts the ordinals in the row that closes this parent. A second fact bearing on the seam this row declines: MT 3:10 opens with words byte-identical to the opening of MT 3:4, and it stands behind an open-section mark on MT 3:9 just as MT 3:4 stands behind one on MT 3:3.
items.both_sides: Near side of the MT 3:9/3:10 junction: MT 3:9 ends on the rebellious-house refrain and carries an open-section mark. Far side: MT 3:10 opens with the very words that open this unit at MT 3:4. The junction is marked in the same kind and the same degree as the junction the row uses for its own opening, so the ground offered against it does not hold. What does keep MT 3:10-3:11 inside the unit is content: both verses carry on the same charge about how the audience will receive the words, and MT 3:11 ends it. The boundary stands; the ground has to change.

suggested_fix.fact: MT 3:9 carries the fourth of the six verses in chapters 2-3 that name the rebellious house

items.claim: The row states that its own splice at MT 3:15 reads the qere. It does not. The variant site in MT 3:15 is the unpointed form standing just after the river name, where the written consonants end in resh; the read form supplied for it ends in bet and carries a dividing accent, and it stands nowhere in the extract. The splice instead quotes the sitting verb from later in the same verse: a different word of the verse, sharing the read form's consonants but pointed with another accent and no part of the dispute. The splice therefore stands clear of the variant, which is exactly what the same writer says correctly of the site at MT 1:8. The rest of the row is sound: the construct at MT 3:14 is one of the seven, weighing it as transit rather than onset is defensible because the journey opened at MT 3:12 runs unbroken to MT 3:15, the paseq at MT 3:13 is the only one in the span, and the span truly carries no parashah mark.

suggested_fix.fact: the ketiv/qere site in MT 3:15 is the word standing after the river name, and the row's splice does not touch it

items.claim: Every Masoretic fact this row asserts holds on the bytes. MT 3:16 carries the word-event in the strict contiguous form and belongs both to the 39 and to the 48 of the first-person family, exactly as the row says; an open-section mark follows MT 3:16; closed-section marks follow MT 3:19 and MT 3:21; and the editorial note at MT 3:20 is what the row calls it, an accepted divergence from BHS agreeing with L on a written and read pairing, with no reading asserted past what the note itself states. The span carries no paseq and no variant site, and the row claims none. Holding the closed mark on MT 3:19 as internal is right: the wicked-man case and the righteous-man case are one paired charge, and MT 3:20 brings no fresh onset device.

items.claim: The row's Hebrew holds throughout. MT 3:22 opens on the hand construct, one of the seven verses that sweep returns, and reading it as a genuine scene opening is right, since the command to rise and go out to the plain follows in the same verse. MT 3:26 carries the fifth and MT 3:27 the sixth of the six verses in chapters 2-3 that name the rebellious house, against twelve book-wide, and the tally of four before MT 3:16 and two after is correct. Paseq is recorded twice on MT 3:27 and a closed-section mark follows it, the only parashah mark in the span. The tier label on the ropes device is exactly right: the word at MT 3:25 and the same word at MT 4:8 differ only in the accent, so they match once accents are set aside and do not match byte for byte. The splice at MT 4:1 is byte-true, and keeping the parent seam between MT 3:27 and MT 4:1 while disclosing the shared device is the honest handling of that tension.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: Whether the rule against a denial placed behind a comma reaches past dateline claims. The same shape stands on device-classification statements in three further rows of this cluster, where a mark is called texture and then, after a comma, not a cut.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: Scoring it once on the dateline, as I did, or on four rows changes what this cluster hands forward, and the suite's own register arm reads none of them as defects, so the scope is not settled by anything I can read.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: Two rows attach a caveat about position inside a verse to a parashah mark, at MT 1:28 and at MT 3:16, and one of them declines on that basis to place the mark relative to the charge in MT 3:17.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: That caveat belongs to paseq. The parashah record fixes each mark as following its own verse, so the caveat withholds a placement the record does carry. It is over-caution rather than a false statement, so I did not score it, but a later lane may read it as a mark claim weaker than its evidence.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: The unmirrored-reference flag on the row covering MT 3:22-3:27 lists MT 4:2 through MT 4:17, none of which that row argues; only MT 4:1 and MT 4:8 are argued there.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: That part of the flag looks like a span named in prose being expanded verse by verse, so answering it as a row defect would install references the row never used.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: MT 2:6 carries the full rebellious-house refrain verse-finally and is not named in the row covering MT 2:1-2:7, whose close rests on the shorter form at MT 2:7.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: It does not move the boundary, but a reader of that row alone would take MT 2:7 for the strongest close of the series in that span when MT 2:6 carries the fuller form.
